questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain four differences between a commercial bank and a central bank.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** A **commercial bank** is a profit-making institution that accepts deposits and gives loans to the public and to firms. A **central bank** is the **apex (head) bank** of a country or monetary zone: for Cameroon, the central bank of the CEMAC area is the BEAC. The two differ in the following ways.

**1. Objective.** A commercial bank aims at **making profit** for its shareholders. A central bank is **not profit-oriented**: it aims at **monetary stability**, the stability of prices and of the exchange rate, and the general welfare of the economy.

**2. Customers.** A commercial bank deals with **individuals, firms and organisations** (it opens accounts, gives loans and overdrafts). A central bank deals mainly with the **government and the commercial banks**, and it normally does not serve the general public.

**3. Issue of notes and coins.** Only the **central bank** has the **sole right to issue legal-tender notes and coins**. A commercial bank cannot issue currency; it creates credit (bank deposits) from the money deposited with it.

**4. Control and policy role.** A central bank **controls the money supply and credit** (through interest rates, reserve requirements and open-market operations), **supervises the commercial banks** and acts as **lender of last resort** to them and **banker and adviser to the government**. A commercial bank carries out the policy of the central bank, it does not make it.

**Other differences:** a commercial bank competes with other banks and has many branches to attract deposits, whereas the central bank is a monopoly and does not compete; the central bank keeps the banks' reserves and **settles debts between banks** (clearing house).

**Conclusion.** The commercial bank serves the public for profit, while the central bank manages the banking system and the money supply in the interest of the nation.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain four functions of money and indicate their solutions to the problems posed by the barter system of exchange.

(12 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** **Barter** is the direct exchange of goods and services for other goods and services, without the use of money. It has serious problems. **Money** is anything generally accepted as a means of payment, and its functions solve these problems.

| Function of money | Barter problem it solves |
|---|---|
| 1. Medium of exchange | Double coincidence of wants |
| 2. Unit of account (measure of value) | No common measure of value |
| 3. Store of value | Difficulty of storing wealth |
| 4. Standard of deferred payment | Difficulty of credit and future payments |

**1. Medium of exchange.** Money is **generally accepted in payment** for goods and services. *Barter problem:* the **double coincidence of wants**: a farmer with plantains who needs a pair of shoes must find a shoemaker who wants plantains at that moment. *Solution:* with money the farmer sells the plantains to anybody for francs and then buys the shoes from any seller, so **buying and selling are separated** and trade becomes easy and quick.

**2. Unit of account (measure of value).** Money expresses the **value of all goods and services in the same unit** (the FCFA), so prices can be compared. *Barter problem:* there was **no common measure of value**; a goat had to be priced in yams, cloth, salt and so on, giving too many exchange rates. *Solution:* every good has **one price in FCFA**, which makes comparison, accounting and planning easy.

**3. Store of value.** Money keeps **purchasing power** from today to a later date, and it can be saved. *Barter problem:* goods such as fish, tomatoes or eggs **perish or lose value** if kept, so wealth could not be saved easily, and bulky goods are hard to store. *Solution:* a person can sell the goods, **save the money** and spend it later (its value is however reduced by inflation).

**4. Standard of deferred payment.** Money is used to settle **debts and contracts to be paid in the future** (loans, rents, salaries). *Barter problem:* it was **hard to fix and repay debts** in goods, because their quality, quantity and value change over time and they may be perishable or disputed. *Solution:* a loan is stated in FCFA and repaid in FCFA later, so **credit and borrowing** become possible, which supports investment.

**Other related points:** money is **divisible** into small amounts (the barter problem of **indivisibility** is solved) and **portable**, so wealth can be transferred easily from one place to another.

**Conclusion.** By acting as a medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value and standard of deferred payment, money removes the main difficulties of barter and increases trade and specialisation.
